newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-WOOD AND TAIT UNFIT FOR THIRD TEST.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-WOOD AND TAIT UNFIT FOR THIRD TEST.

text.p: Inspirational Irish hooker Keith Wood and powerful Scottish wing Alan Tait are among five injured British Lions players unavailable for selection for Saturday's third test against South Africa.
Wood and Tait, who played in both test wins against the Springboks, are still nursing groin injuries from the series-clincher in Durban, Lions media liaison officer Bob Burrows said on Wednesday.
"We will obviously miss both players a great deal. Keith's absence, in particular, is very sad as he has been a great motivational force on this tour."
Burrows said the other injured players were prop Jason Leonard (thigh), Irish number eight Eric Miller (also thigh) and English scrumhalf Kyran Bracken (shoulder).
"Our team doctor James Robson has said Jason will be out of action for four weeks so unfortunately he won't be able to go to Australia later this month with the England side," Burrows said.
"But the doctor expects Bracken's shoulder to clear up in the next two to three days so he might still make the England trip."
England wing Tony Underwood and hooker Mark Regan both advanced their claims for test selection with impressive displays in Tuesday's win over Northern Free State.
They are expected to be the test replacements for Tait and Wood respectively in Johannesburg on Saturday.
Burrows said the Lions selectors would be picking their test team on Wednesday night but would not announce it to the media until Thursday afternoon.
